comment: NTT accounting-parity corpus. See REAL_VECTORS.md for the schema, the synthetic-vs-real distinction, and the procedure to add real ground-truth vectors. The harness (tests/parity.rs) builds a VAA body from each vector, drives 13 guardian observations through the program, asserts the program-computed digest == keccak256(keccak256(body)), and asserts the resulting balance accounts match `expected.balances` EXACTLY (token identity = hub, amount = normalized). All hex fields are 0x-prefixed; 32-byte address fields may be given short (right-aligned is NOT applied: a short hex is left-aligned and zero-padded on the right to 32 bytes, matching how the byte arrays are written on-wire).

vectors.name: native_transfer_lock_unlock
vectors.description: Native transfer: hub native chain == source (emitter) chain. Source side is a native LOCK (credit); dest side is a wrapped UNLOCK/MINT (credit). Token identity is the HUB (chain 2, 0x33..), never the NTT source_token (0xEE..). Amount normalizes 3->8 decimals: 1000 * 10^5 = 100_000_000.

vectors.name: wrapped_transfer_burn_mint
vectors.description: Wrapped transfer: hub native chain (5) is a THIRD chain, distinct from source (2) and dest (10). Source side is a wrapped BURN (debit) so it must be pre-seeded; dest side is a wrapped MINT (credit). Amount normalizes 3->8: 100_000_000.

vectors.name: normalize_scale_up_identity_at_eight
vectors.description: Normalization identity at 8 decimals: raw 12345 @ 8 decimals -> 12345 (no scaling). Native lock/unlock so both sides credit 12345.

vectors.name: normalize_scale_down_truncation_18_decimals
vectors.description: Scale-down with truncation: 18 decimals -> 8 divides by 10^10 (integer, truncating). raw_amount = 1_000_000_001_999_999_999 (~1.000000001999999999e18) -> floor(.../10^10) = 100_000_000 (the sub-1e10 remainder is LOST). Proves precision loss is truncation, not rounding. Native lock/unlock so both sides credit the truncated 100_000_000.

vectors.name: relayer_unwrapped_delivery_instruction
vectors.description: CLOSES THE RELAYER GAP. The VAA emitter is a registered standard relayer; the body payload is a DeliveryInstruction WRAPPING the NTT TransceiverMessage. The hub/peer routing must use the unwrapped DeliveryInstruction.sender_address (0x..0099, distinct from the emitter), while the transfer/digest KEY uses the VAA emitter_address (0x..00AA). The hub is keyed by (emitter_chain, sender) = (2, 0x..0099). Native lock/unlock, amount 3->8 = 100_000_000.
